Canvas.description: The drawing surface's configuration, set by the notation layer's canvas property or by a viewpoint's own canvas. It gives the background paint (by default the canvas colour token), an optional paged layout for printing, fixed bounds, zoom limits and presets, a watermark label drawn under everything, an auto-generated legend, a minimap and the look of the selection outline and resize handles. DISL 0.2 adds the chrome outside the drawing surface: title, header, notices, filters, the empty message, stretching, an initial fit and a legend computed from what is drawn. See section 6.13.

initial.description: The zoom a viewer starts with: a number, or fit, which fits zoom and pan once per viewer and view and never refits on model changes; defaults to default. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

fitPadding.description: The space kept on each side when fitting, as a fraction of the content extent; defaults to 0.05. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

fitWhen.description: Fit when the view opens, or the first time it has content (the default). See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

title.description: The legend's heading. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

from.description: declared (the default, 0.1) shows every entry; drawn shows an entry only while an element in diagram.drawn matches it. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

computed.description: Entries computed from the drawn elements. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

title.description: The title drawn above the drawing surface, outside it, with self bound to the diagram; never zoomed, panned or selected. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

header.description: A band of rows between the title and the drawing surface. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

notices.description: Status notices outside the drawing surface. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

filters.description: User filters by id, whose values are viewer state. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.1.

empty.description: The message shown on an empty canvas. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

fit.description: none (the default) or stretch: scale x and y independently so that bounds, which must be set, fills the pane minus margin; node sizes, strokes and fonts are not stretched. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

margin.description: The space kept around the stretched bounds; defaults to 0. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

ChromeBand.description: A band of text rows drawn between the canvas title and the drawing surface, outside it: not an element, not selectable, draggable or deletable, and not part of layout; the surface's origin is below it. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

rows.description: The rows, labels with self bound to the diagram. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

style.description: The band's style. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

visible.description: Whether the band is shown; defaults to true. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

Notice.description: A status notice drawn outside the drawing surface, such as a truncation banner, with its text, severity, position, visibility and buttons. A notice is not an element; notices stack in declaration order per position. Each truncating budget contributes a built-in notice budget:<id>, and a parse failure the built-in unavailable. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

id.description: The notice's id: a simple identifier, or budget:<id> naming a declared budget. A declared notice with the id of a built-in one (budget:<id> or unavailable) replaces it, and is shown only while the built-in one would be. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

text.description: The notice's text, in the chrome context. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

severity.description: Styles the notice; defaults to info. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

position.description: Where the notice sits, anchored to the surface outside the drawing; defaults to top. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

visible.description: Whether the notice is shown, in the chrome context; defaults to true. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

actions.description: Buttons, each running an operation. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

label.description: The button's label. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

operation.description: The operation the button runs. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

args.description: Values of the operation's parameters, in the chrome context. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

dismissible.description: Whether the viewer may close it; the dismissal is viewer state. Defaults to false. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

style.description: The notice's style. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

Filter.description: A user filter on the canvas, in canvas.filters: a control whose value is viewer state and a keep condition deciding which elements of the types it applies to stay drawn. Filtering never changes the model, findings or undo. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.1.

label.description: Shown on the control; defaults to the id. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.1.

control.description: The control: chips (a list of chosen values), switch (a bool), select (one of options) or search (free text). See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.1.

appliesTo.description: The types the filter can hide; others always stay. Defaults to every node type. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.1.

options.description: The values offered by chips and select, a list in the filter context without self. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.1.

default.description: The value a viewer starts with, a literal or {cel}; defaults to [], false or an empty string by control. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.1.

match.description: For chips: whether an element must match any or all chosen values, and whether the viewer may switch; defaults to any, switchable. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.1.

default.description: Whether an element must match any (the default) or all chosen values. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.1.

userToggle.description: Whether the viewer may switch between any and all; defaults to true. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.1.

keep.description: True when self stays drawn, in the filter context (self, value, match, diagram, env). See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.1.

effect.description: hide (the default) leaves filtered-out elements undrawn, with their relations; dim applies the filteredOut state. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.1.

position.description: Where the control sits, outside the drawing surface. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.1.

EmptyMessage.description: The message drawn centred on an empty canvas, outside the drawing; the toolbox and empty-canvas gestures stay available. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

text.description: The message, in the chrome context. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

when.description: When the message is shown; defaults to the view drawing no element after viewpoint membership and derived elements. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

style.description: The message's style. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

LegendComputed.description: Legend entries computed per drawn element: one entry per distinct key, with its label and swatch taken from the first element of the group. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

key.description: Groups drawn elements into one entry, in the legend context. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

label.description: The entry's text, evaluated on the first element of each group. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

swatch.description: The entry's swatch, evaluated on the first element of each group. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

shape.description: The swatch's shape. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

fill.description: The swatch's fill. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

stroke.description: The swatch's outline colour. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

icon.description: The swatch's icon. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

order.description: The sort key of the entries; defaults to first appearance in persistence order. See DISL 0.2, section 6.13.

Notation.description: The notation layer of a specification: the concrete syntax that says how every node, edge, port and label of the diagram type looks. It holds the theme and fonts, named styles, custom shapes, markers and icons, the notations per node type, edge type and port, the canvas, and defaults for nodes and edges. A visual property resolves from per-element overrides, states, conditions and variants down through styles, supertypes and these defaults to the built-in default. See section 6.1.

textMetric.description: How text is measured for geometry. See DISL 0.2, section 6.5.

TextMetric.description: How text is measured at layout time: host, the host's font metrics (the default, 0.1), or an average advance per counted character. CEL textWidth and textHeight use it, and so every layout input computed with them, so that every runtime and headless layout computes the same layout; drawing measures with the real font. See DISL 0.3, section 6.5.

kind.description: average: every character advances by the same fraction of the font size. See DISL 0.2, section 6.5.

advance.description: The width of one character, as a fraction of the font size. See DISL 0.2, section 6.5.

count.description: What a character is. See DISL 0.2, section 6.5.

lineHeight.description: The line height, as a multiple of the font size. See DISL 0.2, section 6.5.

Tool.description: One entry in the toolbox, used in tool groups and the toolbox library. Its kind says what it does: create a node or edge (the default, inferred from the type it creates), insert a template, run an operation, a generic tool such as select or pan, or a plugin. Further properties set initial attribute values and size, the interaction mode, a shortcut, whether it stays active, and what happens after creation (by default label editing). DISL 0.2 adds a drop table (mode drop), unavailable reasons, and a CreateEnd for the ends a create-edge tool creates. See section 7.2.

label.description: The palette text, a Message in the element context with self bound to the diagram; defaults to the created type's label. See DISL 0.2, section 7.2.

unavailable.description: Why the tool cannot be used now, in priority order, in the element context with self bound to the diagram; while one applies the tool is shown disabled with that reason and refused. A tool of kind operation also inherits its operation's reasons. See DISL 0.2, section 7.2.

drop.description: What a drop (or click) of this tool does, depending on the element under the drop point. See DISL 0.2, section 7.2.

createSource.description: The node created as the source when a connect gesture ends on empty canvas: a type (0.1) or a CreateEnd. See DISL 0.2, section 7.2.

createTarget.description: The node created as the target when a connect gesture ends on empty canvas: a type (0.1), a CreateEnd, or ask. See DISL 0.2, section 7.2.

CreateEnd.description: The node a create-edge tool creates when a connect gesture is released on empty canvas, in createSource or createTarget: its type, initial attribute values and size. Creating the end, the relation, their hooks and snapping is one transaction and one undo step. See DISL 0.2, section 7.2.

type.description: The node type created for the missing end. See DISL 0.2, section 7.2.

initial.description: Initial attribute values, literals or {cel} in the create context, where position is the release point, parent the container under it and other the existing end. See DISL 0.2, section 7.2.

size.description: The created node's size. See DISL 0.2, section 7.2.

DropSpec.description: A tool's drop table (mode drop): a list of drop targets tried in order against the element under the drop point, and what a drop that none matches does. A tool without drop behaves as in 0.1. See DISL 0.2, section 7.2.

targets.description: Tried in order against the element under the drop point; the first whose on matches runs as one transaction. See DISL 0.2, section 7.2.

elsewhere.description: What a drop that no target matches does: create the tool's own type at the drop point (the default), ignore it, refuse it with refusal, or open the diagram context menu at the drop point. See DISL 0.2, section 7.2.

refusal.description: The refusal shown for elsewhere: refuse; context diagram, env, dropTarget and position. See DISL 0.2, section 7.2.

place.description: A parent placement of behavior.placements that chooses where a drop creates the tool's element; with it, targets and elsewhere are not consulted. See DISL 0.3, section 7.2.

ParentPlacement.description: A parent placement in behavior.placements: chooses the parent of a new element by geometry among candidates, and its index among that parent's children. Evaluated in the parentPlacement context. See DISL 0.3, section 9.1.

candidates.description: The elements that may become the parent, a list of Element. See DISL 0.3, section 9.1.

as.description: The name each candidate is bound to in rank; default candidate. See DISL 0.3, section 9.1.

rank.description: A number per candidate; the lowest wins, the first in model order on a tie. See DISL 0.3, section 9.1.

index.description: The new element's index among the chosen parent's children, with parent bound; clamped to their number; default after the last. See DISL 0.3, section 9.1.

whenEmpty.description: With no candidate: root creates the element at the top level when the diagram has no top-level element candidates could return; refuse (the default) refuses with refusal. See DISL 0.3, section 9.1.

refusal.description: The refusal when no parent is chosen. See DISL 0.3, section 9.1.

DropTarget.description: One entry of a tool's drop table: a context tool of any kind plus on, the types of element under the drop point (or canvas) it applies to. Its self is the drop target, the diagram for canvas, and position is the drop point. See DISL 0.2, section 7.2.

on.description: What the entry applies to: node types under the drop point (with their subtypes) and/or the keyword canvas for empty canvas. See DISL 0.2, section 7.2.

label.description: The entry's label, a Message evaluated for the element it is shown on (and item and index inside forEach) each time it is presented. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

visible.description: Whether the entry is offered at all; an entry that is not visible is not shown, while an unavailable one is shown disabled. Element context. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

unavailable.description: Reasons that, while one applies, show the entry disabled with that reason and refuse it; an entry that runs an operation also inherits the operation's. Element context. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

target.description: How the other end of a connect or create-connected entry is chosen: drag (the default and the 0.1 behaviour), pick from a list of candidates, or either. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

candidates.description: The elements a picker offers, a list in the element context; defaults to every element the relation's ends and prevent-constraints admit. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

candidateLabel.description: The text of each picker row, with item bound; defaults to item.label(). See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

pickerTitle.description: The picker's title; defaults to the entry's label. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

emptyText.description: Shown when there are no candidates, as the reason the entry is unavailable. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

forEach.description: A list; the entry is produced once per item, in list order, with item (or the as name) and index bound in its label, visible, enabled, unavailable, args and icon. An empty list produces no entry. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

as.description: The name item is bound as inside forEach; defaults to item. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

args.description: Values of the invoked operation's parameters, from parameter name to Expression; when they give every required parameter, no parameter dialog opens. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

submenu.description: Groups the entries generated by forEach under one submenu with this label. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

ToolGroup.description: A named group of tools in the toolbox palette, used in the toolbox groups list. It has a required id, a label and icon, and lists its tools either inline or by the id of a tool in the toolbox library; nested groups give sub-groups. It can start collapsed, be limited to certain viewpoints, and be shown or hidden by a visible expression evaluated in the diagram context. See section 7.1.

ContextTool.description: One item of a context tool set, shown beside the selected element as the fastest way to grow a diagram. Its required kind is one of create-connected (a new node linked through the relation type in via, outgoing or incoming), connect, create-child (in a slot), operation, delete, duplicate, editLabel, openForm or plugin. Every kind accepts a label, icon, shortcut, enabled condition and position relative to the element. DISL 0.2 adds moveUp and moveDown, visible and unavailable, a picker of existing elements (target pick), and one entry per list item (forEach); DISL 0.3 adds the menu group an entry is shown in (group). See section 7.3.

label.description: The entry's label, a Message evaluated for the element it is shown on (and item and index inside forEach) each time it is presented. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

visible.description: Whether the entry is offered at all; an entry that is not visible is not shown, while an unavailable one is shown disabled. Element context. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

unavailable.description: Reasons that, while one applies, show the entry disabled with that reason and refuse it; an entry that runs an operation also inherits the operation's. Element context. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

target.description: How the other end of a connect or create-connected entry is chosen: drag (the default and the 0.1 behaviour), pick from a list of candidates, or either. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

candidates.description: The elements a picker offers, a list in the element context; defaults to every element the relation's ends and prevent-constraints admit. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

candidateLabel.description: The text of each picker row, with item bound; defaults to item.label(). See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

pickerTitle.description: The picker's title; defaults to the entry's label. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

emptyText.description: Shown when there are no candidates, as the reason the entry is unavailable. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

forEach.description: A list; the entry is produced once per item, in list order, with item (or the as name) and index bound in its label, visible, enabled, unavailable, args and icon. An empty list produces no entry. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

as.description: The name item is bound as inside forEach; defaults to item. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

args.description: Values of the invoked operation's parameters, from parameter name to Expression; when they give every required parameter, no parameter dialog opens. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

submenu.description: Groups the entries generated by forEach under one submenu with this label. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

group.description: The menu group the entry is shown in: consecutive entries of one set with an equal group, or with none, form one group, decided by the entries as declared; a runtime shows the groups in order and sets them apart. The name is not shown. See DISL 0.3, section 7.3.

ContextToolSet.description: A set of context tools shown next to a selected element, declared in the toolbox under contextTools, or under contextMenus for right-click menus. Its for property names the element types it applies to and when adds a condition in the element context; placement chooses around, toolbar, menu or radial presentation. For context menus the runtime adds standard entries such as cut, copy and paste unless standardEntries is false. See section 7.3.

for.description: The element types the set applies to; the keyword diagram opens it on empty canvas (entries see position), and connection on a pending connection (entries see source, target, sourceAnchor and position). See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

runSingle.description: When exactly one entry is available, run it without showing the menu; defaults to false. See DISL 0.2, section 7.3.

FragmentNode.description: A node to be created when a template is inserted, listed in the template fragment nodes. It needs a local ref name, used by other fragment entries in place of an id, and a type; attribute values are expressions evaluated with the template parameters as p. Its at position is relative to the insertion point, in the coordinate system of the target container, with durations relative to the drop time on time axes. See section 7.4.

FragmentRelation.description: A relation to be created when a template is inserted, listed in the template fragment relations. It has a required type and a source and target that name nodes of the same fragment by their local ref names. Its attribute values are expressions, evaluated with the template parameters available as p. See section 7.4.

Template.description: A reusable pre-built fragment, such as a pattern or starter structure, declared by name in the toolbox templates map. Its required fragment lists nodes and relations that refer to each other by local ref names rather than ids; attribute values are expressions evaluated with the template parameters, declared in params, available as p. Templates are placed with a template tool, dragged from a gallery, or offered as starters for a new diagram. See section 7.4.

Toolbox.description: The palette from which users create elements, declared in a specification's toolbox property. It holds ordered tool groups, a library of tools that groups may reference by id, context tools and context menus, templates and starter templates, plus presentation settings such as layout (default list), searchable (default true) and which generic tools are offered (select and pan by default). If the toolbox is absent, the runtime generates one creation tool per concrete node and relation type. See section 7.1.

FieldValidation.description: A field-local validation rule attached to a form field in its validate list. Its rule is an expression over the entered value, and its message is shown immediately when the rule fails, with a severity of error, warning or info. It gives quick feedback in the form but does not replace the specification's constraints. See section 7.5.

timing.description: When the rule is checked: input, as the value is entered (the default and the 0.1 behaviour), or commit, when the dialog is submitted. See DISL 0.2, section 7.5.

FieldParse.description: How a form item accepts typed text: accepts decides whether the text is taken, write turns it into attribute values as one transaction, and refusal is shown otherwise. value is bound to the entered text. Form context. See DISL 0.3, section 7.5.

accepts.description: Whether the entered text, value, is accepted. See DISL 0.3, section 7.5.

write.description: Run as one transaction when the text is accepted. See DISL 0.3, section 7.5.

refusal.description: Shown when accepts is false. See DISL 0.3, section 7.5.

FormItem.description: One item in a form: either a field that edits an attribute, or a container or other item chosen by its kind. A field names its attribute path and optionally a widget (defaulting by attribute type), label, placeholder, options, field-local validation and actions run on change. Other kinds are section, row, tabs, group, static text, divider, a computed read-only value, a button running an operation or actions, a findings list (problems is its deprecated alias) and plugin. See section 7.5.

kind.description: What the item is. findings lists the findings on the form's target; problems is its deprecated alias (section 18), read and never written. type (DISL 0.3) shows and changes the element's type through behavior.retype, its choices options as given, the element's own type among them. See DISL 0.3, section 7.5.

id.description: The row id of a field, computed item or type item, by which a host addresses the row; without it the row id is the attribute, else the label as evaluated. It changes nothing the row shows, edits or refuses. See DISL 0.3, section 7.5.

label.description: The item's label, a Message evaluated in the form context for the edited element. See DISL 0.2, section 7.5.

placeholder.description: The hint shown in an empty input, a Message evaluated in the form context. See DISL 0.2, section 7.5.

display.description: The text an attribute item shows for its value, in place of the widget's rendering of it; a Message in the form context. See DISL 0.3, section 7.5.

parse.description: Makes an attribute or computed item editable as text: what it accepts, what it writes and how it refuses. See DISL 0.3, section 7.5.

optionLabel.description: For a type item: the label of a choice, with item bound to the type. See DISL 0.3, section 7.5.

refusals.description: For a type item: the reasons a value outside the choices is refused, the first that applies shown; self and newValue (the chosen type) are bound. See DISL 0.3, section 7.5.

title.description: The title of a section, group or tab, a Message evaluated in the form context. See DISL 0.2, section 7.5.

confirm.description: The confirmation asked before this runs: a Message (the 0.1 form, which asks every time) or a Confirmation. See DISL 0.2, section 9.5.

readOnlyReasons.description: Why the field is read-only, in priority order, before the attribute's reasons and the edit gate. Form context. See DISL 0.2, section 7.5.

absentText.description: Shown in the field when the attribute is absent; overrides the attribute's. See DISL 0.2, section 7.5.

emptyText.description: Shown in the field when the attribute's value is empty; overrides the attribute's. See DISL 0.2, section 7.5.

showAbsent.description: Whether the row is shown while the value is absent; defaults to true. See DISL 0.2, section 7.5.

initial.description: The value the field is pre-filled with when a dialog opens, evaluated once in the form context (the create context for a create form), with position when invoked at a point. See DISL 0.2, section 7.5.

unavailable.description: For a button: reasons that, while one applies, show the button disabled with that reason and refuse it. See DISL 0.2, section 7.5.

Form.description: A declarative description of editable fields for one or more element types, or for the diagram root, declared by id in the specification's forms. Its usage says where it appears: property inspector (the default), creation dialog, embedded in nodes, popover or bulk editing. It lays out an ordered list of form items and says when edits commit, by default immediately for inspectors and explicitly for create dialogs. Types without a form get a generated one. See section 7.5.

label.description: The title of the form or dialog, a Message in the form context with self bound to the target. See DISL 0.2, section 7.5.

submitLabel.description: The label of the dialog's confirming button. See DISL 0.2, section 7.5.

cancelLabel.description: The label of the dialog's cancelling button. See DISL 0.2, section 7.5.

danger.description: Whether the confirming button is styled as destructive; defaults to false. See DISL 0.2, section 7.5.

QuickFix.description: A suggested correction offered with a problem reported by a constraint, listed in its fixes. It has a label and either actions, executed as one transaction with self bound to the problem's element, or the id of a declared operation to run. A when condition decides whether it is offered; preferred marks the fix used by fix all and the keyboard shortcut, and applyToAll lets it fix every problem of that constraint at once. See section 8.5.

Constraint.description: A single validity rule, written in CEL and listed in the constraints rules. Its required id and rule give the condition that has to hold; kind is invariant by default or a gesture kind (connect, containment, create, delete, placement, change) checked before a user action. Scope says which elements it is evaluated for (default the diagram), severity defaults to error, and enforcement either reports findings or prevents the change. DISL 0.2 adds code, forEach (one finding per item), location, subject and over (model or view); rule is required unless forEach is given. It can offer quick fixes. See section 8.2.

code.description: The code findings of this rule report to users and tools, such as databricks.duplicate-task-key; it replaces x-adp-ruleId and rule ids kept in label or tags. Suppressions stay keyed by id. See DISL 0.2, section 8.2.

over.description: What one evaluation covers: model (the default and the 0.1 meaning) evaluates once per model however many views are open; view evaluates once per view, with view bound, and each finding carries that view's id. See DISL 0.2, section 8.2.

forEach.description: A list evaluated once per scope element; the rule is then evaluated per item, with item and index bound, and yields one finding per item for which when holds and rule does not, in list order. rule then defaults to false (every item is a finding), and enforcement must be report. See DISL 0.2, section 8.2.

location.description: The SourceLocation map (or null) of the finding, when it is not the target element's location() or is more precise. See DISL 0.2, section 8.2.

subject.description: A string naming the undrawn thing the finding is about, such as a triple or a key path. See DISL 0.2, section 8.2.

Constraints.description: The container for a specification's validity rules, declared in its constraints property. It holds the ordered list of constraint rules, named groups that users can enable, disable or re-rate as a unit, default severity and timing for rules, settings that tune the built-in constraints and, in DISL 0.3, the order of the codes findings are listed in. Its blockSaveOn setting defaults to never, so diagrams with problems are still saved and remain loadable. See section 8.1.

order.description: The codes in the order findings are listed: by the position of a finding's code here, unlisted codes last; then the reader's findings in reading order; then by the line of the finding's element, a group of duplicates by its first member. Without it, or empty, findings keep the order of section 8.6. See DISL 0.3, sections 8.1 and 8.6.

BuiltInSetting.description: The settings of one built-in constraint, in constraints.builtIn keyed by its id such as std.references: its severity, whether it is enabled, the code its findings report, the message of its findings, which may be computed from detail, and the refusal it shows when it refuses a gesture, which may be computed from violation, and (DISL 0.3) whether a group of duplicates is reported once. See DISL 0.3, section 8.1.

severity.description: Re-rates the built-in. See DISL 0.2, section 8.1.

enabled.description: Switches the built-in off; defaults to true. See DISL 0.2, section 8.1.

code.description: The code findings of this built-in report, such as timeline.dangling-connection; or {cel} evaluated per finding in the constraint context plus detail, returning such a code. See DISL 0.3, section 8.1.

message.description: The message of this built-in's findings, in place of the runtime's, in the constraint context plus detail (the keys each built-in lists in 8.7). See DISL 0.2, section 8.1.

refusal.description: The refusal this built-in shows when it refuses a gesture, in place of the runtime's, in that gesture's context plus violation (the keys 8.4 lists per built-in). Without it a refusal is worded by the runtime, never taken from message. See DISL 0.2, section 8.4.

oncePerGroup.description: Reports a group of duplicates once, at its second or its last member, rather than at every member after the first: the holders of one id for std.duplicateId, a repeat that allowParallel false forbids for std.endpoints. No effect on any other built-in or case. See DISL 0.3, section 8.1.

SourceLocation.description: A place in a file of the model, which findings and the reader's element locations carry: file, relative to the diagram's subject as FBL defines it and separated by /, and optionally a line, a column and a length. line and column are 1-based; column and length count Unicode code points; column requires line and length requires column. Without a line the location is the whole file. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

file.description: The file, relative to the diagram's subject, with / separators. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

column.description: The 1-based column, counted in Unicode code points. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

length.description: The length of the located text, in Unicode code points. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

Finding.description: One finding as a headless validator writes it, an item of ValidatorOutput. A finding (DISL 0.1 called it a problem) is the result of a rule or of the reader; this JSON form keeps the 0.1 keys constraintId (the finding's constraint), severity, message, elementId, attribute and pointer, and adds code, elementIds (the finding's target), location, subject and view. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

constraintId.description: The id of the rule that raised the finding: a declared constraint's id or a built-in id such as std.unparseable. Suppressions are keyed by it. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

code.description: The code the rule reports to users and tools, when it declares one, such as databricks.duplicate-task-key. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

severity.description: The finding's severity. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

message.description: The message, evaluated and localized. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

elementId.description: The 0.1 key: the id of the first element the finding is about; equal to the first of elementIds when either is present. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

elementIds.description: The ids of every element the finding is about, in order. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

attribute.description: The attribute the finding is about. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

location.description: Where in the model's files the finding is. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

subject.description: A display string naming something that is not drawn, such as a triple or a key path; never resolved as an id. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

view.description: The id of the view a finding of an over: view rule belongs to. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

pointer.description: The JSON Pointer of the record of a DID definition the finding is about; absent when location names a file that is not a DID definition. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

ValidatorOutput.description: What a headless validator writes: a JSON array of findings in the normative order of findings. The object form, with the same array under findings and an optional $schema, lets a stored example name this schema. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

$schema.description: The schema the stored output names. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

findings.description: The findings, in the normative order of findings. See DISL 0.2, section 8.6.

Action.description: One declarative step from a small, closed set, used in hooks, operations, quick fixes, form buttons and field change handlers. Each action is an object with one leading key such as set, unset, create, connect, delete, move, resize, retype, reparent, let, if, forEach, select, reveal, highlight, editLabel, openForm, notify, layout, abort, call or plugin. All values are expressions, and every action may carry a when condition that skips it unless true. See section 9.4.

after.description: A sibling element: the new or reparented element is placed directly after it in its parent's child order; the parent's children must be ordered. At most one of after and before. See DISL 0.2, section 9.4.

before.description: A sibling element: the new or reparented element is placed directly before it in its parent's child order. See DISL 0.2, section 9.4.

place.description: A parent placement of behavior.placements that chooses the parent and index; exclusive with parent, after and before. See DISL 0.3, section 9.4.

after.description: A sibling element: the new or reparented element is placed directly after it in its parent's child order; the parent's children must be ordered. At most one of after and before. See DISL 0.2, section 9.4.

before.description: A sibling element: the new or reparented element is placed directly before it in its parent's child order. See DISL 0.2, section 9.4.

reorder.description: Changes only the order of an element among its siblings, as one step; refused by reorder gesture constraints. Give one of by, after and before. See DISL 0.2, section 9.4.

target.description: The element to move among its siblings; defaults to self. See DISL 0.2, section 9.4.

by.description: A signed number of positions; -1 moves it up (earlier). See DISL 0.2, section 9.4.

after.description: A sibling to place it directly after. See DISL 0.2, section 9.4.

before.description: A sibling to place it directly before. See DISL 0.2, section 9.4.

view.description: Changes viewer state only, for target (default self): never persisted, never on undo, allowed in read-only mode. An operation whose actions are all view, select, reveal and highlight actions is offered in read-only mode and creates no undo step. See DISL 0.2, section 9.4.

collapsed.description: The viewer's new collapsed state of target. See DISL 0.2, section 9.4.

filters.description: New values of the viewer's canvas filters, by filter id. See DISL 0.2, section 9.4.

viewpoint.description: The viewpoint, or variant, the viewer switches to. See DISL 0.2, section 9.4.

refusals.description: Refusals of a layout action: nothingDrawn while the scope holds nothing the algorithm can place (for rows, no element with a drawable extent), unchanged when the layout would change nothing. See DISL 0.3, section 9.4.

Hook.description: A reaction to an editing event, listed in the behavior hooks. Its required id, on and actions say which events it responds to (such as create, change, connect, move, load or save) and the actions to run in order, optionally limited to element types, changed attributes and a when condition. After hooks, the default, run after the change in the same undoable transaction; before hooks run before constraints and may abort. Hooks do not run for remote changes. See section 9.2.

Operation.description: A named, documented command, declared by id in the behavior operations and invoked from tools, context tools, form buttons, quick fixes, shortcuts or menus. Its for property says what it applies to: element types (bound as self), the selection or the diagram. Parameters produce a generated dialog, or a custom form, and are available as p. Its actions run as one transaction, or a plugin implements it; an enabled expression and a confirmation question are optional. See section 9.3.

label.description: The operation's label, a Message evaluated in the operation context without p each time the operation is presented. See DISL 0.2, section 9.3.

unavailable.description: Reasons that, while one applies, make every entry that runs the operation unavailable with that reason. Operation context without p. See DISL 0.2, section 9.3.

confirm.description: The confirmation asked before this runs: a Message (the 0.1 form, which asks every time) or a Confirmation. See DISL 0.2, section 9.5.

simulate.description: A simulated run, played outside any transaction and never on undo; exclusive with actions and plugin. See DISL 0.2, section 9.6.

Simulation.description: A simulated run played over time, the third body of an operation beside actions and plugin: each step computes every taking-part element's state from the previous step's. It runs outside any transaction; its writes never enter undo, mark the document modified, persist, fire hooks or reach constraints, and any committed change ends the run. See DISL 0.2, section 9.6.

for.description: The element types that take part. See DISL 0.2, section 9.6.

state.description: A transient (or viewer) attribute declared on each of those types: the only thing a simulation writes. See DISL 0.2, section 9.6.

initial.description: Each element's state at step 0, in the simulation context. See DISL 0.2, section 9.6.

next.description: Each element's state at the next step, evaluated against the previous step's states (simultaneous update), in the simulation context (self, state, step, p, diagram, env). See DISL 0.2, section 9.6.

until.description: Evaluated after each step; the run finishes when it is true. See DISL 0.2, section 9.6.

stepMs.description: The time between steps in milliseconds; defaults to 700. See DISL 0.2, section 9.6.

maxSteps.description: A hard stop; defaults to 1000. See DISL 0.2, section 9.6.

notice.description: The status notice shown while the simulation runs and after it finishes; dismissing it ends the run and clears the states. See DISL 0.2, section 9.6.

running.description: The notice shown while the run plays. See DISL 0.2, section 9.6.

finished.description: The notice shown after it finishes. See DISL 0.2, section 9.6.

DeletionPolicy.description: The rules for deleting an element of one type, declared per type in the behavior deletion map. Children says what happens to contained elements (delete by default, reparent to the deleted node's parent, or forbid); relations covers attached edges (delete by default, forbid, or reconnect incoming to outgoing edges of the same type); references covers reference attributes pointing at it (unset by default, delete the referencing elements, or forbid). A confirm text asks before deleting. See section 9.5.

confirm.description: The confirmation asked before this runs: a Message (the 0.1 form, which asks every time) or a Confirmation. See DISL 0.2, section 9.5.

Confirmation.description: A confirmation asked before a deletion, an operation or a button runs, in the object form of confirm. It holds the question, a title, the labels of both buttons, whether the confirming one is dangerous, and when to ask: only while when holds and, if count is given, count >= threshold. A plain Message in confirm is a Confirmation with only a message, which asks every time as in 0.1. See DISL 0.2, section 9.5.

message.description: The question asked; it may use count. See DISL 0.2, section 9.5.

title.description: The dialog title; defaults to the operation's label, or Delete for a deletion. See DISL 0.2, section 9.5.

confirmLabel.description: The label of the confirming button; defaults to the runtime's own. See DISL 0.2, section 9.5.

cancelLabel.description: The label of the cancelling button; defaults to the runtime's own. See DISL 0.2, section 9.5.

danger.description: Whether the confirming button is styled as destructive; defaults to true for a deletion and false otherwise. See DISL 0.2, section 9.5.

when.description: Ask only while this holds; absent means always. See DISL 0.2, section 9.5.

count.description: An integer the confirmation is about, bound as count in its texts, such as the number of nodes under a branch. See DISL 0.2, section 9.5.

threshold.description: Ask only when count >= threshold; defaults to 0, so a confirmation asks every time unless raised. Ignored without count. See DISL 0.2, section 9.5.

Behavior.description: What happens in response to user actions beyond direct manipulation, declared in a specification's behavior property. It holds hooks that react to events, named operations, per-type deletion policies, and clipboard, retyping and undo settings. Its maxHookDepth bounds the number of hook executions in one transaction (default 100), so hooks that trigger further hooks cannot run away. DISL 0.2 adds named reasons, the diagram-wide edit gate and standard messages. See section 9.1.

placements.description: Named parent placements, referred to by a drop's or a create action's place. See DISL 0.3, section 9.1.

when.description: Whether the element may become a target type: self is the element and target the candidate type; default true. See DISL 0.3, section 9.5.

reasons.description: Named reasons, declared once and referred to as {reason: id} from any Reason list. See DISL 0.2, section 9.1.

editGate.description: Diagram-wide reasons that, while one applies, withhold every model-changing gesture, tool, operation and form field, with the first applicable reason as the sentence; gestures that write only view data are not withheld. Element context with self bound to the diagram. See DISL 0.2, section 9.1.

messages.description: Standard sentences the runtime otherwise words itself, by id: std.notApplicable (operation context plus operationId), std.readOnly (element context on the diagram), std.atStart and std.atEnd. See DISL 0.2, section 9.1.

LayoutConfig.description: One named layout configuration, used in the layout algorithms map and for containers. Its required algorithm names the layout, such as layered, tree, force, lanes, an ELK algorithm or a plugin; DISL names algorithms but does not define them. Further settings give the main flow direction, spacing in canvas units, edge routing, whether user bendpoints are replaced, pass-through algorithm options, the default scope and whether notes take part. See section 10.

algorithm.description: The algorithm: a name DISL lists (10), of which rowPacked, rows and tidyTree are standard and defined in 10.1 to 10.3, elk:<id> or plugin:<name>. See DISL 0.3, section 10.

rowPacked.description: The options of the standard rowPacked algorithm; only with algorithm rowPacked. See DISL 0.3, section 10.

rows.description: The options of the standard rows algorithm; only with algorithm rows. See DISL 0.3, section 10.

tidyTree.description: The options of the standard tidyTree algorithm; only with algorithm tidyTree. See DISL 0.3, section 10.

RowPacked.description: The options of the rowPacked algorithm: elements keep their rows and are packed along the main axis in order, gap apart, with connected targets after their sources. See DISL 0.3, section 10.1.

keepRows.description: States that rows are kept; rowPacked never changes an element's row. See DISL 0.3, section 10.1.

order.description: The order within a row: start, by the element's start along the packed axis as its base placement gives it; document, model order. See DISL 0.3, section 10.1.

gap.description: The least distance between two elements on a row, in canvas units. See DISL 0.3, section 10.1.

followConnections.description: A relation type whose targets start no earlier than the targetAfter point of their source. See DISL 0.3, section 10.1.

targetAfter.description: The point of a source a target starts after; default sourceEnd. See DISL 0.3, section 10.1.

rowsCovered.description: The number of rows an element covers from its own row, in the element context; default 1. See DISL 0.3, section 10.1.

RowsLayout.description: The options of the rows algorithm: assigns rows only, writing the attributes in writes; the fewest rows the extents allow when every extent covers one row, and a row covered by a taller extent is never swapped. See DISL 0.3, section 10.2.

writes.description: The attributes the algorithm writes, the row first; it changes nothing else. See DISL 0.3, section 10.2.

extent.description: Per type, the extent an element occupies on its row: from and to along the main axis, and the rows it covers from its own row down. In the layoutExtent context; an element whose extent does not evaluate does not take part. See DISL 0.3, section 10.2.

additionalProperties.description: The extent of one type's elements. See DISL 0.3, section 10.2.

clearance.description: The least distance between two extents on one row, in canvas units; default 0. See DISL 0.3, section 10.2.

affinity.description: A relation type that draws linked elements to nearby rows. See DISL 0.3, section 10.2.

ties.description: Between two equally near free rows, lower takes the smaller row number (the default), upper the larger. See DISL 0.3, section 10.2.

swapPasses.description: The most passes of neighbouring-row swaps; default 0. See DISL 0.3, section 10.2.

TidyTree.description: The options of the tidyTree algorithm: a tidy tree in model order, with optional stored rows and drag behaviour. See DISL 0.3, section 10.3.

order.description: children: each element's children in their model order. See DISL 0.3, section 10.3.

parentAlign.description: A parent centred over its first and last child (firstLastCentre, the default) or over its children's extent (childrenCentre). See DISL 0.3, section 10.3.

origin.description: leftmostAtZero (the default) shifts the layout so its leftmost node is at 0; rootAtZero puts the first root's position at 0. See DISL 0.3, section 10.3.

rows.description: Stored main-axis positions shared by siblings. See DISL 0.3, section 10.3.

stored.description: none (the default): every position is computed; y: the top-level elements, and all children of one parent, share one stored main-axis position. See DISL 0.3, section 10.3.

minGap.description: The least gap between a parent's far edge on the main axis and the near edge of its children's row, in canvas units. See DISL 0.3, section 10.3.

drag.description: What dragging an element does. See DISL 0.3, section 10.3.

carry.description: subtree: everything beneath moves with the dragged element; node: it moves alone. See DISL 0.3, section 10.3.

across.description: reorder: dropped past a sibling's centre, the element is reordered among its siblings in the model. See DISL 0.3, section 10.3.

down.description: row: the dropped main-axis position is stored for the row and everything beneath it. See DISL 0.3, section 10.3.

Layout.description: The automatic layout settings of a specification, declared in its layout property. It names layout configurations under algorithms, chooses the default one used by the Arrange command, sets layouts inside containers of a type, and says when layout runs automatically (manual by default) and which user positions survive it (pinned elements by default). Layout never changes coordinates bound to attributes, such as a task's start date. See section 10.

MigrationStep.description: One step of a migration, written as an object with a single step key and an optional doc. Steps rename, delete or retype types, rename, delete, set or convert attributes, transform a whole attributes map, convert stored view coordinates, rename ports and slots, or call a plugin. Expressions run in the migration context, which sees raw records as maps rather than typed elements, because the old definition does not conform to the new metamodel. See section 11.9.

Migration.description: An upgrade from older language versions, listed in the persistence migrations. Its from property is a version range, to is the version it produces, and steps is a non-empty ordered list of migration steps. Migrations run on load, before validation, in version order; a failing migration aborts loading, and the original file is not modified until the user saves. See section 11.9.

IdStrategy.description: How elements get their ids, in persistence.ids: the default strategy for every type (the 0.1 properties strategy, prefix, expression, stable and pattern, plus encoding, ephemeral, reason and suffix), per-type rules in types, what happens to missing ids on reading, and how ids are compared. Nodes, relations and views share one id space; of elements sharing an id the first in reading order keeps it. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

strategy.description: How ids are made: the 0.1 generation strategies, or derived, whose id is the value of expression evaluated in the identity context and recomputed after reading and at the end of every transaction. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

encoding.description: The text form of uuid-v4 and uuid-v7 ids: hex (the 0.1 form, the default), base64url (22 characters) or base36 (25 characters); ids stay opaque strings. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

prefix.description: Prepended to generated ids, one string, or at the top level a map from type to string (0.1); not applied to cel or derived results. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

expression.description: The id, a string: required for cel (evaluated once, on creation, in the create context) and for derived (in the identity context). See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

stable.description: Ids never change once assigned, even if natural keys change. Defaults to true. Has no effect on derived ids, which always follow their expression. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

ephemeral.description: Whether the id identifies the element within one reading of the model only: a boolean, or an Expression evaluated in the identity context. An ephemeral element is never stored as view data, a style override, a suppression or a reference. Defaults to false. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

reason.description: The refusal shown when a gesture would store an ephemeral id, in the element context with self bound to the ephemeral element; defaults to the runtime's sentence. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

pattern.description: The allowed id syntax; defaults to ^[A-Za-z0-9_.:#-]{1,128}$. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

suffix.description: How a generated cel or natural id is made unique: {n} is replaced by the smallest integer n >= 2 that makes it unique. Defaults to -{n}. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

types.description: Per-type id rules, keyed by type reference; each overrides the default for that type and its subtypes that have no rule of their own. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

missing.description: What a runtime does with an element read without a usable id: assign gives it a new id, written with the next save (the default); ephemeral treats it as ephemeral. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

compare.description: How ids are compared for lookups, references, duplicate detection and view keys: exact (the default) or ignore-case, by Unicode default case folding, keeping the first spelling read. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

IdRule.description: The id rule of one type in persistence.ids.types, overriding the default for that type and its subtypes (the nearest rule in the type's linearisation wins). It holds a strategy, including derived, whose expression runs in the identity context; the encoding of generated UUIDs; ephemeral, for ids that do not survive a re-reading, with the reason given when a gesture would store one; and prefix, stable, pattern and suffix as for the default. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

strategy.description: How ids are made: the 0.1 generation strategies, or derived, whose id is the value of expression evaluated in the identity context and recomputed after reading and at the end of every transaction. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

encoding.description: The text form of uuid-v4 and uuid-v7 ids: hex (the 0.1 form, the default), base64url (22 characters) or base36 (25 characters); ids stay opaque strings. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

prefix.description: Prepended to ids generated for this type; not applied to cel or derived results. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

expression.description: The id, a string: required for cel (evaluated once, on creation, in the create context) and for derived (in the identity context). See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

stable.description: Ids never change once assigned, even if natural keys change. Defaults to true. Has no effect on derived ids, which always follow their expression. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

ephemeral.description: Whether the id identifies the element within one reading of the model only: a boolean, or an Expression evaluated in the identity context. An ephemeral element is never stored as view data, a style override, a suppression or a reference. Defaults to false. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

reason.description: The refusal shown when a gesture would store an ephemeral id, in the element context with self bound to the ephemeral element; defaults to the runtime's sentence. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

pattern.description: The allowed id syntax; defaults to ^[A-Za-z0-9_.:#-]{1,128}$. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

suffix.description: How a generated cel or natural id is made unique: {n} is replaced by the smallest integer n >= 2 that makes it unique. Defaults to -{n}. See DISL 0.2, section 11.5.

Persistence.description: How the diagrams users draw are stored as DID definitions, declared in a specification's persistence property. It chooses the serialization format (json by default), encoding and file split, how ids are generated, how records and keys are ordered, number precision and timestamps, which view data and style overrides are kept, metadata, how the specification is referenced, migrations, collaboration, and import and export conversions. The aim is byte-identical output from any two conforming runtimes. DISL 0.2 moves ids to IdStrategy and adds viewer state to view. With format fbl the model is instead a body in another tool's format, read and written through an FBL binding (FBL, the Format Binding Language), and the DID writer settings are not given. See sections 11.1 and 11.2.

binding.description: The FBL binding that reads and writes the model when format is fbl: a URI reference to an FBL document followed by '#' and the binding's name, or an inline FBL Binding. See section 11.2.

typeMap.description: Only with format fbl: the binding's types mapped onto the metamodel, keyed by the binding's type name; without it, the binding's types and attributes are the metamodel's. See DISL 0.3, section 11.2.

viewer.description: View-data kinds held per viewer: never persisted, never on undo, changeable in read-only mode, not shared with other viewers and not readable from deterministic contexts. See DISL 0.2, section 11.6.

initial.description: The value each viewer kind starts with when a viewer first opens a view, from kind to a literal or {cel} in the element context; collapsed without one starts false. See DISL 0.2, section 11.6.

revealExpands.description: Whether revealing or selecting an element inside a collapsed container expands its collapsed ancestors; defaults to true. See DISL 0.2, section 11.6.

TypeMapEntry.description: How one type of an FBL binding maps onto the metamodel, in persistence.typeMap. See DISL 0.3, section 11.2.

as.description: What the binding's entries of this type become: diagram (their attributes are the diagram's), header or unreadable (kept out of the model; unreadable ones reported by std.unreadableEntry), or a metamodel type. See DISL 0.3, section 11.2.

attributes.description: The binding's attribute names mapped to metamodel attributes; source and target make a reference attribute an end of a relation, id the element's id, and null leaves the attribute out of the model. Unlisted attributes keep their names. See DISL 0.3, section 11.2.

hostAttributes.description: Attributes the binding reads and writes that are not attributes of the model. See DISL 0.3, section 11.2.

ViewKind.description: A kind of view data: the 0.1 kinds a view may store (bounds, waypoints, anchors, labelOffsets, collapsed, zIndex, rotation, params, ports, viewport, guides, pinned, settings) plus the viewer-only kinds selection, filters and viewpoint. persistence.view lists the kinds a view stores and the kinds each viewer holds; a kind may not be in both. See DISL 0.2, section 11.6.
